feedback: The submitted app link opens a restricted Google Doc, and the brief is also inaccessible. I need a public hosted app link and a viewable brief before I can assess the work.
tested: Google Doc: 'You need access' in signed-in browser; Docs connector 403; brief not available to connector.
limitations: No app screens or flows observable.
name: Shaikh Madiha

feedback: The kitchen-to-recipe idea is useful and the screens are coherent. But adding an item shows success without adding it to inventory; too much stops at demo data. I expected one reliable add → expiry → recipe flow before this many features.
tested: Landing, dashboard, inventory search/details, manual add, recipes, planner, community, analytics, settings, admin. Added test item: success toast, still 12 inventory items, search finds nothing.
limitations: OCR, external store connections, donations and payments not exercised. Demo flow assessed.
name: Kashvi Khanna

feedback: The vault theme, timed locks and hints fit together, and the full game actually works. I completed all five locks, restarted into different questions and checked the failure state. Good attention to the experience; tighten the end-screen copy and keep key actions easier to reach.
tested: All five locks solved; correct-answer progression, final code/success/rank, restart with different questions, hint consumption, timeout and wrong-answer failure.
limitations: Share action not sent; audio audibility not independently measured.
name: Saffa Ahmad

feedback: A focused idea with a complete challenge-to-reward loop. XP, streaks and badges update and survive refresh; good attention to the experience. I expected clearer matching between the selected mood and the challenge, and more depth in the recommendations.
tested: Home → three preferences → challenge → accept → complete → profile. 15 XP, one completion and badge retained after refresh. Chill/5min/₹0 returned a Social challenge.
limitations: One preference combination tested; broad recommendation quality and streak rollover not exhaustively assessed.
name: Darshan Rajeev Kulkarni

feedback: The capture → review → saved connection flow is well thought through, and the record survives refresh. Follow-ups, interview tracking and the assistant make this useful beyond a dashboard. I expected more care in the generated output: the next-action text exposes an unresolved ${c.eventType} placeholder.
tested: Text note parsed into Alex Example / Example Company, editable review and saved profile retained on refresh. Dashboard, contact detail, follow-ups, interviews, assistant and settings inspected; assistant returns due contacts.
limitations: Local browser storage disclosed. Camera, uploads, calendar integration and sending messages not exercised.
name: Nupur Jethi

feedback: A clear, usable utility with a restrained interface. Adding a reminder, retaining it after refresh, triggering it and rescheduling with a quick preset all work. I expected clearer explanation of background delivery and recurrence so users know when they can rely on an alarm.
tested: Created synthetic task using in5m; persisted reload; moved to Past/triggered at due time; rescheduled via preset back to Upcoming. Manual time fill displayed new value then reverted on save.
limitations: Audible alarm, background/closed-tab delivery and daily/weekly recurrence not verified. Manual time editing could not be reliably exercised with the browser controls; not treated as an app defect.
name: Ram Bhardwaj
Nemil Doshi
feedback: The idea-validation journey is clear and the quick feasibility check works. But generating the full report crashes to a blank screen, and competitor analysis stays empty. I expected a reliable report with explainable evidence before adding more dashboard sections.
tested: Guest entry, quick feasibility score, full validation form, saved validations, competitors and settings. Full-report generation crashed with undefined overallScore; reload recovered dashboard and saved validation listing.
limitations: Report could not be read after generation; accuracy and sources of AI scores not established.

name: Pranjal Jain
feedback: The brand, photography and product presentation feel considered. The quiz, ring configuration and saved bag work. I expected tighter recommendation logic: an engagement-ring quiz returned a pendant, and the recommended ring opened at a price above the selected budget.
tested: Five-step quiz, results, product detail, carat change, add to bag, reload persistence, checkout form and ring-builder entry. ₹50–85k engagement preference returned pendant and ₹68k ring opening at ₹104.5k default configuration.
limitations: No order or payment submitted. Try-on and full custom-ring completion not verified.

feedback: The job-search journey and next-action focus are clear, and the landing page is polished. But the guided demo is a sequence of screenshots; the working product requires sign-in. Give me a guest account or a usable demo so I can assess execution rather than marketing screens.
tested: Landing, preview tabs, guided-demo step change and sign-in page inspected. Guided demo displays images; capture routes to account creation.
limitations: No guest access or supplied credentials. Authenticated capture, pipeline, AI and persistence cannot be scored.
name: Ribhav Mangla
Abhinav Kaushik
feedback: The import → leak diagnosis → recovery sprint is a useful, working flow. My two test records changed the totals correctly and the sprint tracked actions. But refreshing discarded the imported dataset and returned to the demo. I expected saved work and clearer support for the recovery probabilities.
tested: All six navigation screens inspected. Pasted two synthetic leads totalling ₹3,000, mapped columns, analysed and completed sprint with ₹2,000 recovered and one contacted. Reload reset dataset to IronCore Fitness demo.
limitations: CRM integrations, actual outreach and payments not exercised. Simulator screen inspected; keyboard change did not visibly alter value.

name: Sana Bhagat
feedback: The five-step quiz, product swaps and saved routine are clear and work. But the core budget promise fails: selecting under ₹1,000 produced a ₹3,514 routine, with no explanation of monthly cost versus purchase cost. I expected the recommendations to respect the answers, not just repeat them in the heading.
tested: Synthetic normal skin / dryness and dullness / low sensitivity / under ₹1,000 / moderate climate. Generated ₹3,514 routine, swapped cleanser, saved ₹3,519 routine and confirmed after reload. Ingredients and personalisation screens inspected; checker accepts sample actives.
limitations: UI behaviour assessed, not clinical suitability or safety. No products purchased. Total repeats the same moisturiser for morning and night.

name: Harshit Agrawal
feedback: The interface is composed and the recommendations respond to a specific request, with useful reasons. Saving a title works and survives refresh. I expected more honest availability labels: the streaming buttons are generic search links, and the precise match percentages need an explanation.
tested: Requested a light family film under two hours; four relevant results with runtimes and reasons. Added Paddington 2, checked library, reloaded and confirmed saved title. Home, Discover, library and search inspected.
limitations: Streaming availability, trailers, sharing and broad recommendation accuracy not independently verified; provider links point to search pages.

name: sahil singh
feedback: The game collection goes beyond a menu: tic-tac-toe recognises wins and restarts, and the hockey paddle and puck respond to dragging. The presentation is clear but fairly standard. I expected the play area to fit the screen better; the physics games put the player's controls below the fold.
tested: All five game pages opened. Completed a PvP tic-tac-toe win and restart; rock-paper-scissors move submitted; Pen Fight and Carrom boards rendered; Air Hockey paddle drag changed paddle and puck positions.
limitations: Full Pen Fight/Carrom matches, hockey scoring, bot difficulty and cross-device controls not exhaustively tested.

name: Naadir Singh Dhaliwal
feedback: A thoughtful family-memory concept, with warm typography and readable chapters. The timeline and chapter expansion work, but the experience is mostly a prefilled family story. I expected a demonstrable recording → transcription → saved chapter flow, plus clearer evidence behind the capture percentage.
tested: Home, story timeline, expanded chapter, book preview and Ask screen inspected. Audio control changes state; empty question submit checked. No recording/import workflow found in the available navigation.
limitations: No question sent to family or microphone access granted. Audio audibility, scheduled calls and new-memory generation not verified. Score reflects observable demo.

name: Anudeep Gupta Samayamantula
feedback: The daily song game is focused and works: skipping unlocks more audio, search selects a song, and a correct answer updates persistent stats. Good follow-through on the core loop. I expected a more robust audio experience and playable past songs to give the history screen a purpose beyond a list.
tested: Instructions, intro playback control, skip from 2 to 3 seconds, autocomplete Shaky, correct submission, stats and history. One win on guess2 retained after reload.
limitations: Audio player state verified but audibility not independently measured. Daily rollover, loss state and sharing not exercised.

name: Aashi Bhansali
feedback: The arcade identity is consistent, and there is a working progression loop behind it. Cyber Cricket records a result, awards coins and updates persistent stats. Good follow-through. I expected favourites to influence the library as promised, and a clearer explanation of the global rank shown before any play.
tested: Guest onboarding with Viper Grid favourite, library categories/locks, Cyber Cricket full round → score3,000 / +370 coins / balance620. Stats, profile and settings inspected; state retained after reload. Favourite was not pinned first.
limitations: Locked Viper Grid and Grid Collapse gameplay not reached; Neon Marbles not played. Global rank not verified as live.

name: Nitilaksh Bhaskar
feedback: The visual theme is consistent and the one-tap mechanic actually works. I could start, swing across the screen, lose and retry; the best score survives refresh. I expected a little more onboarding and clearer feedback on what ended the run so the difficulty feels learnable.
tested: Start, animated game, pointer tap produced visible cross-screen grapple arc, game-over scores7 and3, retry, best7 retained after reload.
limitations: Long-session difficulty balance, mobile touch and audio not exhaustively assessed.

name: Sree Sree Simhadri
feedback: The task manager is usable beyond the seeded screen. Adding and completing a task updates the list and calendar consistently, and both survive refresh. Good attention to the core workflow. I expected less duplication between the full calendar and side planner, and clearer product identity than the default welcome/version copy.
tested: Created synthetic task with notes, retained after reload, completed it, checked Completed and Calendar views, reloaded again. Settings, sync and backup panels inspected; local mode disclosed.
limitations: Cloud login, push delivery, voice capture, backup download and complex nested-project operations not exercised.

name: Sri Krishna
feedback: A focused party game with clear instructions and a usable tap fallback. Deck selection, the timer, correct/skip actions and the final score all work. Good attention to the actual play experience. I expected stronger feedback for skipped titles and a round history so players can review more than the correct guesses.
tested: Instructions, deck/era/difficulty choices, Bollywood/Easy, tap mode, 60-second round, correct and skip taps, late hint, results showing one correct /10points, change deck.
limitations: Phone tilt, physical group play and external score sharing not tested.

name: Nikhil Lall
feedback: The taste quiz, cocktail detail and saved collection form a usable flow, and bookmarks survive refresh. The visual style is consistent. I expected evidence behind the exact match percentages and the claim that all listed lounges serve the selected drink; the venue cards describe unrelated signature cocktails.
tested: Answered first four quiz questions and used offered early-results action; French75 result, alternate Cucumber Basil Smash, bookmark3 retained after reload, saved collection/profile and lounge list inspected.
limitations: No alcohol purchase or table reservation made. Venue menus, distances and match-score accuracy not independently verified. Full ten-question variant not exercised.

name: Kanak Agarwal
feedback: The tiny neighbourhood and moving avatars give this a distinct personality. People, chat and status panels open, but the saved avatar accessory resets on refresh. I expected durable customisation and a demonstrable friend-to-friend interaction; location detection is still marked coming soon.
tested: Map/place interactions, Zara conversation panel, avatar editor, status composer. Selected headphones and saved; after reload accessory selection returned to None. Location auto-detect disabled/coming soon.
limitations: No messages/status pins sent to others and no location permission granted. Multi-user presence and delivery not verified.

name: Archit Kumar
feedback: The dashboard is organised, but this feels like a one-shot first pass with too little testing. Create Campaign does nothing, and a study-planner request with a ₹1–2k budget returns a skincare plan with 20 creators. I expected one connected, input-aware campaign flow before nine dashboard sections.
tested: All nine navigation sections inspected. Create Campaign click produces no form after wait. AI planner accepts campus study-planner input and ₹1,000–2,000 budget but outputs fixed beauty themes, dermatologists,15 micro/5 macro creators and8.5–12M reach.
limitations: No creator outreach, approvals or payments submitted. Seeded brand/account and historic campaign data assessed as demo.

name: Mansi Malhotra
feedback: The sitcom concept and visual direction are strong. But this feels like a one-shot set of screens with little continuity: I joined as Review Demo and selected Storyteller, yet the app made me Wingman and showed Alex's prefilled profile and 2,450 points. I expected one real join → mission → result loop.
tested: Landing, join form with synthetic details, role selection, character, missions, arena, results and achievements. Chosen Storyteller did not carry through; profile shows Alex Mercer and seeded achievements. Mission progress and score prefilled before play.
limitations: No lobby messages, audience votes or real participant interactions sent. Multi-user synchronisation not verified.

name: Preksha Rathi
feedback: The retro photobooth direction is distinctive, and four uploaded images render into a strip with working filter and background controls. This has more substance than a static mock. I expected a clearer export guard: the app reports memory saved even with zero photos. Final downloaded-image quality still needs verification.
tested: Uploaded four synthetic PNGs through all slots; buffer advances0/4→4/4 and enables configuration. Film grain, gradient and caption controls inspected in live strip. Empty export reports MEMORY SAVED; full export button exercised.
limitations: Download event could not be confirmed with available browser controls; resulting file contents, cropping and print quality not verified.

name: Aaryan Bansal
feedback: The pantry-to-recipe idea is clear and the public screens look tidy. But tomato-soup and mushroom-risotto links both open the same Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl. That basic mismatch makes this feel like an untested first pass. I expected correct recipe routing and a guest pantry flow before adding nutrition tracking.
tested: Home, pantry sign-in gate, guest recipe search and two distinct recipe links. Tomato search narrows list, but tomato-soup and mushroom-risotto detail URLs display identical quinoa content.
limitations: Pantry and logged-meal functionality require authentication; no credentials supplied. Scores reflect public demo only, not authenticated features.

name: Shabareesh Parlakota
feedback: The travel positioning and visual presentation are considered, and the preference form is clear. I could not complete native date entry reliably in this review environment, so I am leaving execution unscored rather than calling the app broken. A sample generated itinerary would make the core experience easier to assess.
tested: Landing, destination autocomplete Japan, India origin, traveller type/count and budget controls. Date fills changed DOM values but did not reliably update the form; Continue remained disabled.
limitations: Native date control/tooling limitation prevented reaching itinerary generation. No booking or payment attempted.

name: Snehal Yutika
feedback: The feedback → issue → action journey is well thought through, and the AI pipeline produces new themes with supporting customer quotes. But the action I added disappears after refresh, along with the generated analysis. I expected durable results and clearer separation between seeded trend figures and actual analysis.
tested: All primary navigation screens, sample100-review pipeline completion, changed issue themes, evidence-backed recommendation and Add to Action Center. Active count5→6; reload returns5 and removes generated action. Generated themes also reset to seeds.
limitations: CSV upload, Amazon sync and team invitations not tested. No real business workflow executed; generated action added only to demo.

name: Ashima Tyagi
feedback: The brief-to-caption flow works, and the saved caption survives refresh. But the generated pop-culture reference turns into thousands of repeated instructions, overwhelming both the result and history screen. I expected output validation and sensible length limits before adding this many tone and platform options.
tested: Synthetic first half-marathon/rain/friends brief; Humour+Inspire, English, caption generation. Relevant caption and hashtags returned; Save Caption persisted in History after reload. Explore/Profile inspected. Reference field degenerates into repeated guidelines/context text.
limitations: Image upload, copy clipboard contents and external social publishing not tested. No post shared.
